messages.subject: D-RUG updates: Weekly worktimes and future presentations...
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG updates: Weekly worktimes and future presentations...
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,
Just a heads up, we haven't quite sorted out a schedule for this quarter, but we will be checking the https://d-rug.discourse.group/ site regularly, and I'll try to be online between 10am and 12pm on Thursdays to answer questions along with other D-RUG coordinators.

We are working on setting up a few zoom presentations this quarter, please stay tuned.

In addition for those folks who are interested or using slack, let me know and I can add you to a slack channel that was started awhile ago. It hasn't gotten much use, but may be a nice way to chat/ask questions.

In the meantime, I hope everyone is doing well, both mentally and physically. Be well, take breaks, and hope to see everyone in person in the not-to-distant future.

Thanks,
Adios,
Ryan
--

"When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the universe."
John Muir (My First Summer in the Sierra, 1911)
-----------------------------------------------------
Ryan Peek, PhD (he/him)
Aquatic Ecologist, Post-Doctoral Researcher
Center for Watershed Sciences, UC Davis
ryanpeek.github.io <http://ryanpeek.github.io>
@riverpeek
530.754.5351

messages.subject: R for Spatial Workshop: #maptimeDavis & Davis R Users Group
messages.subject_clean: R for Spatial Workshop: #maptimeDavis & Davis R Users Group
messages.body_plain:
#maptimeDavis and the Davis R Users Group are pleased to announce our “R for Spatial” workshop April 28, 2020 from 10:00am-12:00pm with speaker Leah Nagel via Zoom!  This workshop will focus on the newly updated SF package.

Attendees are welcome to watch or follow along on their own R Studio console.  If you plan to follow along, please review the Getting Started section of Leah’s ReadMe on her GitHub repository for this workshop to install the necessary software and R packages: https://github.com/ldnagel/spatial-r-for-gis-users

We will assume attendees have an introductory understanding of non-spatial R programming to allow time to focus on spatial functions and a basic understanding of GIS concepts outside of R (desktop GIS experience, for example).  Leah has a script to help get you started or refresh your memory if it’s been a while since you’ve worked in R:  https://github.com/ldnagel/spatial-r-for-gis-users/blob/master/scripts/r-basics-code.R  Please contact Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu if you’d like help finding other introductory materials.

Zoom Link:   https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/ (link at the bottom of the page)

#maptimeDavis <https://github.com/maptimedavis/MaptimeDavis>, the Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/>, and the Davis R Users Group <https://d-rug.github.io/> are supported by the  UC Davis DataLab <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/> and by the contributions and participation of our community.  Please send questions to Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu

Upcoming Workshops & Meetings (Tuesdays 10:00-12:00 via Zoom):

28-Apr   #maptimeDavis:  R for Spatial <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/virtual-workshop-maptimedavis/> with speaker Leah Nagel

5-May   Spatial Sciences Research Cluster:  More Spatial SQL <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/virtual-research-cluster-spatial-sciences-3/>

12-May #maptimeDavis:  Mapbox <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/virtual-workshop-maptimedavis-2/> with speaker Megan Danielson from Mapbox

19-May Spatial Sciences Research Cluster:  Topic To Be Decided <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/virtual-research-cluster-spatial-sciences-4/>

26-May

2-Jun     Spatial Sciences Research Cluster:  Topic To Be Decided <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/virtual-research-cluster-spatial-sciences-5/>

The Davis R Users Group <https://d-rug.github.io/> holds weekly work sessions online on Thursdays from 10:00AM–12:00PM.

messages.subject_clean: Helpers for R for Spatial Workshop
messages.body_plain:
I’m looking for a couple of volunteers to be helpers at the R for Spatial workshop on Tuesday.

We need people who can answer questions about R in general and people with spatial R experience.  You would be responsible for helping to monitor the chat window, answering questions in the chat that can be answered there, and bringing up questions to the instructor for things she needs to answer.  You don’t need to be an expert, just have some knowledge and be willing to help.  I used this model for the QGIS workshop a few weeks ago and it worked pretty well.

If you can help, please send me an email.
